messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: p99 tail latency spike for customer 'nebula' on single-tenant cluster nebula-prod (region us-west-2). Auto-alert threshold breached (p99 > 2.5s)
alex: picking this up — saw the alert, joining. any immediate customer reporting?
tanvi: nebula SRE just pinged support, they reported timeouts in streaming clients and some partial responses.
ops-bot: paging oncall-sre (pager duty) — page sent at 6765432101
oncall-sre: I'm on it. can someone post recent tail metrics and a quick description of workload?
carmen: quick summary — sudden jump in concurrent streaming sessions + many long prompts (~>8k tokens avg) from a single API key. single-tenant so they have reserved capacity but concurrency spiked 3x. p95 stayed OK, p99 shot to ~6s and some streaming stalls reported.
mike: stack traces show a lot of KV cache misses + some backpressure in the streamer queue. suspect longprefix + high fanout (clients opening multiple parallel streams per user).
tanvi: reproduced a small repro locally with long prefix churn; we see continual KV eviction thrash. throughput drops and stall windows at tail.
oncall-sre: steps to mitigate short-term? can we limit concurrency per-API-key or fallback to a lower-capacity model variant?
alex: immediate mitigations I can run: 1) apply soft concurrency throttle for nebula route, 2) enable prefix caching warmup for their hot keys, 3) route excess to cheaper variant with smaller KV working set.
alex: throttling command (will apply 2 min):
```
redwoodctl routes update nebula-route --max-concurrency 120 --apply --owner alex
```
oncall-sre: go ahead on throttle. also open a canary to the smaller variant:
```
redwoodctl rollout start nebula-route --variant small-kv --percent 20 --reason "emergency tail mitigation"
```
carmen: started cache warmup script against their hot keys, pushing prefixes into KV. script logs: `warmup: pushed 312 hot-prefixes in 62s`
mike: seeing immediate drop in queue lag from 450ms -> 160ms after cache warmup. p99 trending back down to ~3s but still noisy.
ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: rollout to small-kv at 20% started at 6765432180
deply-bot: (simulated) new variant healthy checks passing 20/20
oncall-sre: good. alex, please keep throttling in place and escalate if p99 doesn't drop under 2.5s in 10m. Carmen/Mike continue monitoring KV miss rate.
tanvi: also noticed a spike in long-prompt rate from nebula's key: they launched a user-side job that fanout-requests multiple prompts in parallel. asked support to pause the job — they acknowledged.
support (via external): Nebula confirms they paused the batch job at 6765432235.
mike: after pause + warmup + throttle, p99 is at 2.2s and streaming stalls dropped to near zero. latency histograms attached in logs: `p50 120ms / p95 780ms / p99 2.2s`
oncall-sre: continuing to observe. can we keep 20% variant and throttle for 30m then reassess? also need post-incident followup items.
alex: agreed. immediate action plan: maintain throttle + variant canary + KV warmup for 30m. open incident ticket and assign postmortem.
carmen: tentative root cause: combined long prefix working set + sudden high fanout from a single API key causing KV cache eviction thrash and streamer queue backpressure. single-tenant reserved capacity helped but concurrency semantics overwhelmed optimizations.
tonvi: (note) we should add a safety cap per-api-key for concurrent streaming sessions and an automated fallback to variant when KV miss rate > 30% for > 60s.
oncall-sre: creating handoff to daytime oncall for continued monitoring. I'm staying for escalation if it regresses.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied (throttle + small-kv canary + cache warmup). Customer paused job. Monitoring p99.
alex: quick commands run during triage:
```
# throttle
redwoodctl routes update nebula-route --max-concurrency 120
# start canary
redwoodctl rollout start nebula-route --variant small-kv --percent 20
# run cache warmup
./tools/warmup_kv.sh --route nebula-route --prefix-file nebula-hot-prefixes.txt
```
mike: logs showing brief stall window earlier:
```
[6765432155] streamer queue len=820 backpressure=1.0 kv_miss_rate=0.73
[6765432162] evict_count=1400 kv_pop_ms=128
[6765432170] stall window start
[6765432186] stall window end
```
car­men: (typo fix) carmen -> carmen :)
alex: want a handoff note for the postmortem: timeline, mitigation steps, root cause hypothesis, proposed automation (per-key throttle, KV-miss-triggered fallback, longer-lived warmup for long-prefix workloads).
oncall-sre: I'll create the incident channel and assign owners. Tagging participants for followup: @alex, @tanvi, @mike, @carmen.
ops-bot: incident channel created: #inc-6765432100-nebula-p99. oncall-sre transferred the ownership at 6765432345.
alex: leaving notes in the ticket and will draft the postmortem. thanks all. :wave:
oncall-sre: closing active mitigation loop; monitoring for 15m then we'll transition to postmortem.
ops-bot: Incident updated to STATUS=mitigated, DURATION=~6m, CUSTOMER_IMPACT=partial streaming stalls/timeouts, SLO_BREACH=p99>2.5s.
